candidates.teaser: An octopus has something most creatures can only dream of — and it stops working every time it swims.
candidates.video_title: Octopuses Have 3 Hearts — And 2 Stop When They Swim
candidates.video_description: Octopuses have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it to the body. But the moment they start swimming, the main heart stops beating — which is why octopuses prefer crawling. Nature's ultimate design flaw or masterpiece?
candidates.script: What if your heart stopped every single time you ran? That's exactly what happens to an octopus. These creatures have three hearts — two pump blood through the gills, and one delivers it to the rest of the body. But the moment an octopus starts swimming, that main heart literally stops beating. That's why octopuses prefer crawling along the ocean floor instead of swimming — they actually get exhausted and faint if they push it too hard. Oh, and their blood is blue. So the question is: is the octopus the most fascinating animal alive, or the most poorly engineered?

candidates.topic: Napoleon was once attacked by rabbits
candidates.teaser: One of history's most feared military commanders was completely defeated — by the most unexpected enemy imaginable.
candidates.video_title: Napoleon Was Defeated by an Army of Rabbits
candidates.video_description: After the signing of the Peace of Tilsit in 1807, Napoleon organized a celebratory rabbit hunt. But instead of wild rabbits, his staff had gathered hundreds of tame ones — and they swarmed straight at Napoleon, overwhelming his entire party. Even his marshals couldn't stop them.
candidates.script: Napoleon Bonaparte survived countless battles and conquered most of Europe — but one morning in 1807, he was completely overwhelmed and had to flee. His own celebration rabbit hunt turned into chaos. After signing a major peace treaty, Napoleon arranged a festive hunt and ordered hundreds of rabbits to be collected. The problem? His staff gathered tame rabbits instead of wild ones. The moment they were released, instead of running away, they swarmed directly toward Napoleon and his men — climbing boots, scaling jackets, ignoring every attempt to drive them off. Napoleon himself had to retreat to his carriage. So what finally stopped the great conqueror: cannon fire, or hungry bunnies?

candidates.teaser: There's something sitting in your kitchen right now that is, technically, radioactive — and you've probably eaten one today.
candidates.video_title: Bananas Are Radioactive — Here's Why It's Fine
candidates.video_description: Bananas contain a naturally occurring radioactive isotope called Potassium-40. Scientists even created a unit called the 'Banana Equivalent Dose' to measure radiation exposure. You'd need to eat around 10 million bananas at once for the radiation to be dangerous.
candidates.script: The fruit sitting on your kitchen counter right now is technically radioactive. Bananas contain a naturally occurring radioactive element called Potassium-40, and scientists take it so seriously they created an actual unit of measurement called the Banana Equivalent Dose — used to help people understand low-level radiation exposure. Now before you panic, you would need to eat roughly ten million bananas all at once for the radiation to actually harm you. In fact, you're exposed to more radiation from a single chest X-ray than from eating bananas your entire life. But here's what nobody tells you — Brazil nuts are actually far more radioactive than bananas. So should we rename the scale?

candidates.topic: Time moves faster at your head than your feet
candidates.teaser: Right now, time is literally passing at a different speed for different parts of your body — and Einstein predicted it.
candidates.video_title: Time Moves Faster at Your Head Than Your Feet
candidates.video_description: Einstein's general relativity predicts that time moves faster farther from a gravitational source. Your head, being slightly farther from Earth's core than your feet, ages a tiny bit faster — about 90 nanoseconds over a lifetime. GPS satellites must account for this daily.
candidates.script: Right now, time is moving faster at the top of your head than at the bottom of your feet. This isn't science fiction — it's Einstein's theory of general relativity. Gravity warps time, and since your head sits slightly farther from Earth's gravitational center than your feet, time ticks just a tiny bit quicker there. Over a full lifetime, your head ages roughly 90 nanoseconds more than your feet. It sounds trivial, but this effect is so real that GPS satellites — which orbit far from Earth's gravity — must constantly correct for time dilation or navigation systems would drift by miles every single day. So technically, taller people are aging faster. How does that make you feel?

candidates.topic: There is a color the human eye cannot see — Stygian blue
candidates.teaser: Scientists discovered a color that physically cannot exist in the real world — but your brain can be tricked into seeing it.
candidates.video_title: There's a Color Your Eyes Can't See — But Your Brain Can
candidates.video_description: Stygian blue is a color that cannot physically exist as light — it would require negative brightness. Yet in lab experiments, scientists have tricked the human brain into perceiving it through specific optical illusions targeting cone cells. It's a color that exists only in the mind.
candidates.script: There is a color that cannot physically exist as light anywhere in the universe — yet scientists have made people see it. It's called Stygian blue, and it would require something called negative brightness to actually appear in nature, which is impossible. But researchers found that by overstimulating specific cone cells in your eye with a carefully designed optical illusion, your brain gets confused and generates this forbidden color entirely on its own. People who've seen it in lab experiments describe it as something they've never seen before and can't quite explain afterward. Your eyes aren't cameras — they're storytellers. So what other colors might your brain be hiding from you right now?
